title: Enterprise value storyline and risk FAQ
author: Ari Patel
content:
Overview
--------
This document provides a compact, sales-ready value storyline and a prospect-facing risk & security FAQ for enterprise deals. It combines crisp positioning, a competitive brief, a recommended pitch-deck narrative, a pricing guidance snapshot, a short customer case study, and an appendix with a prospect briefing checklist. Use this as the canonical briefing for AEs and solutions engineers when engaging mid-market and enterprise buyers.

Positioning & core messages (elevator + three proof points)
-------------------------------------------------------
Elevator: Redwood Inference provides predictable, production-grade LLM serving that lowers inference unit cost while preserving latency and reliability across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.

Three proof points:
- Economics-first runtime: Intelligent batching, KV/prefix caching, and quantization profiles reduce per-token cost by 20–50% on typical retrieval-augmented and classification workloads.
- Production SLOs and fallbacks: 99.9% availability SLA for Dedicated plans with multi-region fallback policies and automatic model-variant failover.
- Unified dev experience: One API + SDKs across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private — same prompts, same routing controls, and integrated observability.

Competitive brief (summary for objection handling)
------------------------------------------------
Target competitors: Cloud provider managed endpoints, single-vendor LLM APIs, and open-source inference vendors. Key differentiators we lead with: predictable reserved capacity (Dedicated), private VPC/on-prem options, and first-class tooling for cost/latency tradeoffs.

Quick comparative matrix (high level)
-----------------------------------
Provider | Strength | Risk to buyer | Redwood counter
---------|----------|---------------|----------------
Major cloud AI | Vendor lock-in + integrated infra | Expensive at low latency, limited quantization guidance | Offer Dedicated + cost modeling; show benchmarked unit-costs
LLM API #1 | Ease of use, model breadth | No private deployments, weak SLAs | Emphasize Private & Dedicated + 24/7 enterprise support
Open-source self-host | Low license cost | Operational toil, long time-to-market | Pitch Redwood as "managed serving runtime + ops"
Specialized vendor | Good for custom models | Narrow ecosystem, limited tooling | Show our model catalog + runtime kernel selection benefits

Pitch deck narrative (6 slides recommended)
-----------------------------------------
1) The problem: inconsistent latency & exploding token costs in production
2) The solution: Redwood — unified runtime + routing + observability
3) How it works, at a glance: dedicated pools, caching, routing, fallbacks (diagram)
4) Customer outcomes: latency, cost, reliability metrics (case study highlight)
5) Security & compliance: VPC, KMS/HSM, audit logging, SOC/ISO roadmap
6) Commercial & next steps: pilot scope, success metrics, timeline

Speaker notes: focus early on cost predictability (quarterly commitments), and finish with the pilot success metrics (P0 latency, throughput, and cost targets).

Pricing guidance (rules of thumb for early negotiations)
-----------------------------------------------------
- Hosted API: best for rapid POCs and proof-of-value. Typical sticker: pay-as-you-go token pricing with soft quotas; recommend 3–6 month runway credits for larger proof-of-value projects.
- Dedicated: fixed monthly reserved GPU pools. Suggested anchor prices by customer size (internal only):
  - SMB / dev teams: 8–16 GPU equivalent reserved pools — start conversation at $35k/month commit.
  - Mid-market: 32–64 GPU pools — anchor at $120k/month; include 3% commit discount for annual terms.
  - Enterprise: custom sizing with SLA & premium support. Expect multi-quarter negotiations.
- Pricing levers to highlight: committed throughput, burst capacity blocks, observability retention add-ons, and premium SLAs.
- Quick commercialization tactics: start with a 6–8 week pilot (shared sandbox Dedicated or VPC Hosted), success criteria: 95th percentile latency < target, cost/unit <= baseline, end-to-end evaluation prompts.

Short customer case study: FinTechNova (for live conversations)
-----------------------------------------------------------
Context: FinTechNova is a payments platform deploying real-time fraud scoring and conversational customer support.
Engagement: Dedicated deployment with VPC peering, quantization profiles applied to ranking models, and a rollout over 10 weeks.
Results (measurable outcomes):
- Latency: 95th percentile inference latency reduced from 380ms → 210ms (45% improvement).
- Cost: per-1M-token inference spend reduced by 38% through batching and KV caching.
- Reliability: production cutover with zero critical incidents and automated fallback to CPU-based model variants during a GPU maintenance window.
Owner & contact: Solutions Engineer: Daniel Ortiz; Account Exec: Priya Sharma.

Security & Risk FAQ (sales-facing answers to common prospect questions)
---------------------------------------------------------------------
Q: Can you run inside our VPC or on-prem?
A: Yes. Redwood Private supports customer-managed VPC deployments and an on-prem packaging option. We provide a private control plane and can integrate with KMS or HSM for key management.

Q: What audit and logging capabilities are available?
A: Audit logs record model version, request id, timestamp, and route. Customers can configure log retention (30/90/365 days) and export to their SIEM (S3/Cloud Storage or syslog).

Q: How do you protect training or production data from leaking into model weights or other tenants?
A: We recommend model isolation (dedicated pools) for sensitive workloads. For hosted models we enforce tenant isolation in the runtime, and we provide prompt/response redaction hooks. We also support customer-supplied models in Private deployments.

Q: What compliance attestations do you hold or plan to hold?
A: Currently: SOC 2 (Type II) in scope for Hosted and Dedicated customers. Roadmap: ISO 27001 and FedRAMP readiness assessment (Q3 2026). For regulated customers we provide documentation packages and supported audit requests.

Q: What are your SLA commitments and how are incidents handled?
A: Dedicated SLA: 99.9% monthly availability. Hosted: best-effort SLAs with availability reporting by token bucket. Incident process: 24/7 support for enterprise accounts, standard runbook escalation, and post-incident RCA delivered within 72 hours.

Q: How do you mitigate model regressions and quality drift?
A: Redwood Optimize integrates prompt sets and automatic quality monitors with alerts for regressions. We support canary rollouts (traffic split), A/B experiments, and automatic rollback policies.

Prospect briefing checklist (step-by-step)
----------------------------------------
1) Prep: gather three representative prompts and baseline logs (latency, throughput, cost).
2) Scope pilot: define P0 latency (95th), cost/unit target, and failure tolerance.
3) Architecture decision: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private and model variant selection.
4) Security review: KMS/HSM, network topology, and retention policies.
5) Commercial terms: pilot credits, commit level, SLA add-ons.
6) Run pilot: 6–8 weeks, weekly syncs, metrics dashboarding.
7) Convert: share handoff doc with SRE + product for cutover.
